card: Adds the p2p_transport_v2_receive fuzz target to exercise BIP324 V2Transport byte reception. Today, fuzzing does not test V2Transport against arbitrary or corrupted byte streams past the initial key exchange. The author notes this target constructs streams containing arbitrary bytes mixed with corrupted handshake segments in variable slice sizes, covering all receive states and failure paths without finding crashes under ASan/UBSan.
evidence: PR description: "No fuzz target feeds V2Transport bytes that an honest peer would not send past the v2 key exchange."

PR description: "It reaches every v2 receive state and the failures on the way to them. I ran it for about 13 minutes in total from an empty corpus, with libFuzzer and the address and undefined sanitizers, and it found no crash."
problem: Existing fuzz targets do not feed arbitrary or corrupted bytes to V2Transport past the initial BIP324 key exchange, leaving the transport's post-handshake deserialization and receive state machine under-fuzzed.

risk.why: Touches only a fuzz target file, so a bug would only fail CI or waste fuzzing cycles.

summary: Adds a new fuzz target, p2p_transport_v2_receive, to exercise the BIP324 V2Transport receive path. The target constructs input streams from arbitrary bytes and valid or corrupted handshake components, delivering them in variable chunk sizes to cover all receive states and error conditions.
